title: Compact facade for evented chat iterator and retry contracts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Users integrating streaming chat in Python often write brittle glue to turn event streams into convenient sync/async iterators while handling cancellation, deterministic replay for retries, and idempotent sink behavior. Current SDK helpers are powerful but verbose, and several teams duplicate small adapter logic. We need a compact, battery-included facade that covers common patterns with clear retry contracts and minimal surface area.
proposal: Introduce a lightweight ChatEventIterator facade that exposes both a sync iterator and an async __aiter__ wrapper backed by a single event source. Key features: stable event IDs for each emitted event, an explicit CancellationToken object for cooperative cancellation, a replay cursor that is stable across retry attempts, and an explicit idempotency contract for consumer sink side-effects. Provide a small set of built-in adapters (string-merged content, delta-assembly, function-calls) and a simple opt-in callback API for users who need low-level events.
api_sketch:
from redwood_sdk.streaming import ChatEventIterator, CancellationToken

# sync usage
it = ChatEventIterator.from_stream(response_stream)
for event in it.sync_iter(cancellation_token=CancellationToken(timeout=5.0)):
    if event.type == 'delta':
        print(event.text)
    elif event.type == 'function_call':
        handle_function_call(event.payload)

# async usage
async for event in ChatEventIterator.from_stream(response_stream).aiter():
    # event.id is stable across retries, event.cursor can be used for replay
    await consumer.handle(event)
backwards_compatibility_notes: Default behavior will be additive: we provide facade wrappers that sit on top of existing low-level stream parsers. Existing SDK users are unaffected unless they adopt the new facade. The facade will not change existing wire formats; it only adds stable 'event_id' and 'cursor' metadata at the SDK layer where absent.
migration_notes: Document a two-line migration: replace custom assembly loops with ChatEventIterator.from_stream(stream) and switch to the built-in delta_to_text adapter for most use cases. Examples in docs/ and Quickstart notebook will show sync and async patterns.
testing_plan: Unit tests for: stable event_id generation across identical streams, cancellation token behavior (timeout and cooperative cancel), replay cursor correctness across simulated transient errors, idempotency helper tests for sink adapters. Integration tests run in CI with a mocked stream server that can inject disconnects and duplicate events. Add fuzz tests for event ordering and partial deltas.
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit events: sdk.stream.iterator.created, sdk.stream.iterator.cancelled, sdk.stream.iterator.replayed, sdk.stream.iterator.error with tags: adapter, cancellation_reason, replay_attempts. Add a dashboard to track median time to first event and replay rates per adapter.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal alpha for SDK team and two partner apps (billing UI, agent service) for 2 weeks. Phase 2: public beta in py-sdk-3.4 with docs and examples. Phase 3: stable default in py-sdk-3.5 if no major issues. Feature gated via environment variable REDWOOD_PY_SDK_STREAM_FACADE for the first two phases.
acceptance_criteria: API implemented and exported in python SDK package
Unit and integration tests passing in CI
Docs page with sync/async examples and migration guide published
Two partner apps verified behavior and no regressions observed
